props.gloss_en: two walls according to their law, and the third even a handbreadth
R' Shimon: three walls according to their law, and the fourth even a handbreadth
in what do they disagree? the Rabbis hold the written form is authoritative; R' Shimon holds the read form is authoritative
the Rabbis hold: the written form [of the text] is authoritative
R' Shimon holds: the read form [of the text] is authoritative
[as written] בסכת, בסכת, בסכות -- here are four
take away one for [the mitzva] itself, three remain: two according to their law [and a third]
and the halakha came and reduced the third and set it at a handbreadth
[as read] בסכות, בסכות, בסכות -- here are six
take away one verse for [the mitzva] itself, four remain: three according to their law [and a fourth]
the halakha came and reduced the fourth and set it at a handbreadth
or say: all agree the read form is authoritative, and they disagree over this -- one master holds its covering requires a verse, the other that it does not
or say: all agree the written form is authoritative, and they disagree over this -- one master holds the halakha comes to reduce, the other that it comes to add

or say: all agree the halakha comes to reduce and the written form is authoritative, and they disagree over whether first occurrences are expounded -- one master holds they are, the other that they are not (the text does not say which master is which)
R' Shimon's reason is from here: 'and there shall be a sukkah for shade by day from the heat, and for refuge and cover from storm and from rain' (Yeshayahu 4:6)
where does he set that handbreadth? Rav: he sets it opposite the one that projects
Shmuel in Levi's name: he sets it opposite the one that projects; and so they rule in the beit midrash
he makes it a wide handbreadth and sets it less than three handbreadths from the wall
and anything less than three [handbreadths] adjacent to the wall is as if joined (lavud)
a sukkah made like an alleyway is valid
and that handbreadth he sets on whichever side he wishes
he makes it a board of four [handbreadths] and a bit and sets it less than three from the wall
Rava: and it is permitted only by a form of a doorway
some say, Rava said: and it is permitted also by a form of a doorway
some say, Rava said: and it also requires a form of a doorway
Rav Ashi found Rav Kahana making a wide handbreadth and making a form of a doorway

challenges.gloss_en: אמרי ליה רב כהנא ורב אסי לרב: ויעמידנו כנגד ראש תור?! שתיק רב -- let him set it opposite the ראש תור; Rav was silent (the text does not adjudicate, and 7a.2 adduces support for Rav)

objections.gloss_en: ומאי שנא התם דקאמרת סגיא טפח שוחק, ומאי שנא הכא דקאמרת בעיא פס ארבעה? -- why does a wide handbreadth suffice there and a board of four is required here?

answered_by.gloss_en: התם דאיכא שתי דפנות כהלכתן -- סגי ליה בטפח שוחק; הכא דליכא שתי דפנות, אי איכא פס ארבעה -- אין, אי לא -- לא: there, where there are two walls according to their law, a wide handbreadth suffices; here, where there are not, a board of four yes, otherwise no

objections.gloss_en: לא סבר מר להא דרבא, דאמר רבא: וניתרת נמי בצורת הפתח? -- on that version the form of a doorway alone suffices, so why make the wide handbreadth too?

answered_by.gloss_en: אנא כאידך לישנא דרבא סבירא לי, דאמר רבא: וצריכא נמי צורת הפתח -- I hold like the other version of Rava, that it also requires the form of a doorway (= p_rava_tzricha_gam)
